chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Norman Granz's Ellington tapes and the lost Carnegie Hall Black, Brown and Beige
summary: Jones believes Granz will release more Ellington material and recalls the black-market Carnegie Hall tapes he lost in a fire.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I don't know. He'll probably release it someway, because I went to his office one day. You know, I was doing a string date with Milt Jackson, and Norman had so much stuff on Duke that he'd gotten from Mercer that hadn't been released. So I imagine he's going to release all this stuff.
Yeah, he's already released some of it, I know, that he got from Mercer.
I had one thing and I lost it in a fire and I'm so sorry, but that's one of the reasons I -- I had the original "Black, Brown, and Beige" off the Carnegie Hall stage.
Well, that -- Fantasy has put that out.
Yeah. The one that was recorded there at Carnegie Hall?
With Duke talking and all that?
I think so, yeah. Actually mine just came and I haven't played them yet, but --
Because Ben was in the band then.
Ben, Otto Hardwick. Yeah, that was --
It was material they got from Mercer.
Yeah, well, that was in World War II.
